Been giving this some thought and I don't think a lot of the changes are necessarily bad:

Buffed:

Hard Light - +10% buff, immune to stability nerf, immune to damage falloff nerf.

Necrochasm - Cursebringer buff, magazine buff, immune to stability nerf

No Land Beyond - +20% buff to Master precision damage, Master lasts 8 seconds, buff to weapon handling, sights fixed.

All other AutoRifles: - This REALLY needed to be done. +10% buff Less starting stability Damage falloff starts closer

All Scout Rifles +5% damage for medium to high RoF guns + Magazine size Reduced Final Accuracy when hip firing

All other Rocket Launchers: +Blast Radius Buff +Grenades and Horseshoes proximity reduced.

Little Impact:

Sidearms - No mention of sidearm changes AT ALL.

Icebreaker - Time per round increased 3 seconds. 18 seconds total. Never more than 8 seconds away from your next shot, had been 5 seconds. If you're continually waiting for a full gun, you're using it wrong. Fire 4 fast shots, keep 2 in reserve, allow #3 to regenerate, fire, regen, fire, regen, fire. If you're feeling confident, you could even start with 5 shots, keep 1 in reserve and continually shoot #2 every 8 seconds.

Black Hammer - Ammo buffed to 18 rounds, White Nail now pulls from inventory, not a problem due to ammo drops and synths.

Gjallarhorn - Wolfpack round damage reduced no word on how much of a reduction rumor is 20%, but that's ONLY on the Wolfpack rounds.

All Sniper Rifles: Final Round only buffs precision damage, not base. If you're using a sniper and not doing precision damage, you're doing it wrong.

Nerfed:

All Fusion Rifles: Not sure why they did this, did they NEED to make FR's worse? Projectile speed reduced Accuracy buffed for short range Accuracy nerfed for long range Slow charge, high impact = Decreased range

Last Word - Range reduced, stability reduced, range reduced, immune to hip firing nerf.

Thorn - DoT reduced 2/3rds, but stacks * 5. This may end up being a buff, hard to say yet. It takes 3 shots to equal the same DoT you had with 1, but there's now a possibility of increasing it 66% with 2 more shots. For the things that survive 3 Thorn shots that will be a good thing.

Hawkmoon - Luck in the Chamber and Holding Aces = only 2 bonus perks per round. Holding Aces = +2 rounds. Luck in the Chamber nerfed 3%.

All other Hand Cannons: As a class, hand cannons are pointless again. Damage falloff starts closer Accuracy reduction on aiming Reduced Final Accuracy when hip firing - Magazine size Reduced base optics Aiming emphasises width over depth

All Pulse Rifles: They nerfed AutoRifles to push people to Pulse Rifles, now they're pushing them back? + magazine size 2.5% nerf PvP bursts to kill capped at 2 or 3 Less starting stability

All Shotguns: - This seems to be the worst change of the bunch. It more or less takes shotguns off the table again but there should be a good alternative. I had been keeping an Arc Shotgun for fallen captains and a Void Shotgun for Minotaurs. But when I leveled up the Vestian Dynasty, I switched that to my Captain weapon. If they introduce Void and Solar Sidearms, that could replace shotguns.

10% Damage nerf Reduced range Range damage boost + high initial range = less effective Shot Package nerfed 30% Rangefinder nerfed 15% Precision Damage nerged 10%
Weapons 2.0 Changes ranked Best to Worst:

Frankly, I'm really excited to see all the weapon changes. I want to see fusion ruffles become a viable choice next to shotguns, and with these changes it looks like they will be again. Auto rifles now seem like they're going to actually be comparable to pulse rifles again (feels weird saying that).

Personally, I really want hand cannons to be very short range, very high impact weapons. Slightly longer range than the current shotguns, and slightly higher impact than HC's currently have, with slightly reduced stability. That would make them a good short range choice compared to the long range scout rifles and medium range pulse rifles, and the high ROF, lower impact, decent stability Auto rifles.

That almost sounds like the approach they're trying to go for with HC's, but they're doing it all wrong.

I think what it really comes down to is that the hand canon weapon class should never have been a primary weapon class. They are too good from too varied of ranges, making them the optimal choice for most situations. If they did not exist, the two different types of auto rifles would both be viable, and the long range Scott rifles would be used more often as well. I don't think pulse rifles would change much, because they've finally reached a good middle ground.

As a special weapon class, hand cannons could have been very similar to shotguns (short range power house), but require more accuracy to get the kill off (less target acquisition, more skill). There should be 2 types: slow and heavy, with only a few rounds per magazine (3 or 4), and able to take another player down in 2 headshots, but very slow ROF and with slow reload; and the snappy weaker version, with 5 to 7 shots per clip, takes down a player with 3 to 5 headshots, has pretty high ROF, but low stability at faster firing speed, but a speedy reload. Both would have about the range of fusion rifles

This Is How The Wind Shifts - Silverstein

The whole album is a concept of mirrors essentially. Each track has a mirror track that deals with an opposing idea, or different side of a story, etc. The pattern of mirror tracks is 1/8 - 2/9 - 3/10 - 4/11 - 5/12 - 6/13 - 7/14. There's a track about a battered wife who finally gets the courage to leave, and its mirror track is about the husband after she is gone. Then there's another track about a man whose wife dies and how he is coping with it, and the mirror track is about the ghost of the wife watching her husband struggle through it. There are two tracks on the album that are the title tracks, one is called "This is How" and the other is called "The Wind Shifts". They are tracks 4 and 11, the center tracks in each half of the album. If you play the two tracks over the top of each other they line up perfectly to create a whole complete song. It's a seriously brilliant album, I've never found another quite like it.
